newsitem.title: UK: London freight - Holidays limit activity.
newsitem.headline: London freight - Holidays limit activity.

text.p: Various world holidays have limited freight activity, but despite this some positive features have emerged for owners.
Fresh panamax period timecharter activity was noted and brokers saw potentially firmer conditions for modern craned tonnage on the Continent.
Grain activity for handies was said to be increasing in the Plate and to a lesser extent in the U.S. Gulf.
On the other hand, the caper market has remained limp.
The BFI was up 9 points to 1434 and the Baltic handy index remained unchanged at 1008.
GRAIN - Many brokers believe handy-size rates in the Plate may be about to turn in owners' favour.
The 1972-built Ailsa was booked by Continental for a prompt shipment of 26,000 wheat up river and Necochea to Thessaloniki at $22.50 basis 2-1.

Toepfer fixed 30,000 wheat river Plate/Alexandria on subjects, and have also fixed on subjects 30,000 grains 55' U.S. Gulf/Portugal for Feb 17-25 at $14.50. They also quoted fresh enquiry for 30,000 heavy grain U.S. Gulf/Casablanca for Feb 20/27.
Soufflet quoted a new order of 50,000 barley Southampton/Jeddah for Feb 21-25. There were also rumours of timecharter business being completed although confirmation could not be obtained.
The 1976-built Johny C 54,614 dwt was linked with D'Amato (possibly in direct continuation) delivery Continent Feb 17-20 for 5-7 months at $7,500 daily.
Pioneer may have taken a 50,000 dwt vessel delivery Gibraltar for 3-5 months at close to $7,300 daily.
There was incomplete reports of the 1975-built Kavako 65,003 dwt fixed for period basis spot delivery Gibraltar.
Another was the Bright Days 68,676 dwt fixed from the Continent to the Far East at $15,000 daily, but it was not known if this trip was loading from the Continent or U.S. Gulf.
In the east, Pacrim continued to take tonnage for Australian grain to Iraq. The Vori 34,544 dwt was booked delivery spot Malaysia, redelivery passing Muscat outbound at a steady $8,000 daily.

MINERALS - A very quiet caper market featured reports that HMM fixed Ormond 187,028 dwt for Posco tender business delivery Passero early March for a trip with Brazilian ironore to S.Korea at close to $20,250 daily.
British Steel were thought to have fixed Mineral Dragon for 110,000 tonnes ironore Ponta da Madeira/Port Talbot for March 7-14 in the low $5.00's but confirmation was unavailable.
In the east Samsun were believed to have booked Esplanade 140,000 dwt delivery S.Korea end Feb for a Queensland coal round trip but again details were lacking.
Panamax activities in the east were largely confined to period negotiations. Pan Ocean covered Oinoussian Navigator 64,368 dwt delivery Taiwan mid Feb for 5-7 months at $10,500 daily.

Antonis I Angelicoussis 69,346 dwt open Japan end Feb and El Flamenco 69,351 dwt open Qingdao Feb 20-28 were both said to have been offered $11,500 daily for 12 months but were holding out for about $11,750 daily.

HANDY-SIZES - Brokers say that modern craned tonnage of about 42,000 dwt has been fixed privately at firmer rates from the Continent to the Far East, possibly for about $12,500/13,000 daily, and larger vessels for more.
Alcinoe 34,500 dwt was understood fixed delivery prompt Continent trip Bangladesh at close to $11,900 daily.

E.D. and F. Man have been active fixing vessels delivery Spain for transatlantic business on private terms and have also booked the Western bulk-relet Golden Condor 43,000 dwt delivery U.S. Gulf trip Chile at $9,750 daily.
Holidays have largely curtailed activity in the Far East.
